newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro currency to be guided by price stability - Wicks.
newsitem.headline: Euro currency to be guided by price stability - Wicks.

text.p: There is broad agreement among European Union policy-makers that a future common currency should be one that reflects price stability, EU monetary committee chairman Sir Nigel Wicks said on Tuesday.

Speaking to a committee of the European Parliament, Wicks said: "I think there is a strong determination to have a price-stable currency...We want a currency which is well respected on international currency markets."
The international role of the single currency, the euro, is one of the main items on the agenda for the EU monetary committee in the coming months, Wicks said.
Regarding future relations between the euro and currencies not participating at the start date in 1999, Wicks said it was conceivable that one could see short-lived bouts of volatility.
A new Exchange Rate Mechanism "can't necessarily in the short-term guarantee currency stability," he told the parliamentary group.
But should governments outside a monetary union pursue economic policies geared towards low inflation, one would expect currency stability to eventually follow.

Under a single currency it was also possible to envisage long-term interest rate differentials among those inside monetary union, reflecting perceived differences in credit risk and market imperfections, he added.
